comprendre-les-parcours.title: Understanding the pathways to Europe
comprendre-les-parcours.subtitle: Clearly distinguish between university studies, vocational training and work-related mobility.

sections.heading: Higher education (Bachelor’s, Master’s, Doctorate)
sections.body: The academic pathway is for holders of the baccalaureate or a university degree who wish to pursue theoretical and research-based education at an accredited public or private university.
bullets: Requires official recognition of your secondary-school or higher-education diploma
Requires a certified language level (often B2 or C1 in the language of instruction)
Involves proof of funds in a blocked account or of an official scholarship, according to the regulations of the host country

sections.heading: Vocational training (e.g. Ausbildung in Germany)
sections.body: Work-based vocational training combines classes at a vocational school with paid practical work in a company for 2 to 3 years.
bullets: An excellent command of the country’s language is essential (at least a solid B1, or B2)
Apply directly to training companies, with no intermediary fees
An official training contract is required before any consular procedure

sections.heading: Skilled professional mobility
sections.body: For professionals who already hold a recognised higher-education or technical qualification and verifiable experience.
bullets: Prior equivalence or recognition procedure for professional qualifications
Strict compliance with the national rules of the labour and immigration ministries

preparer-son-dossier.title: Preparing your application file with care
preparer-son-dossier.subtitle: Good document practices for putting together an authentic, clear and compliant file.

sections.heading: Absolute authenticity of documents
sections.body: Any forged or inaccurate document leads to immediate refusal and lasting bans with the consular authorities. WAHHF makes every applicant aware of the importance of a 100% authentic file.
bullets: Gather your original transcripts and diplomas
Have documents legalised or authenticated only by official administrations
Have your documents translated by recognised sworn translators

sections.heading: CV and cover letter
sections.body: Each European country has its own presentation conventions (for example the clear tabular format in Germany, or the Europass format).
bullets: Present your real background honestly and clearly
Explain how your past studies fit with the project you are aiming for
Have your texts proofread during the WAHHF support workshops

apprendre-la-langue.title: Learning the language of the country: the key to independence
apprendre-la-langue.subtitle: Why language skills always come before the administrative procedures.

sections.heading: Language protects you and makes you independent
sections.body: Leaving without mastering the language of the host country exposes you to isolation, academic failure and insecurity. That is why WAHHF puts language learning first and foremost.
bullets: Regular practice of listening, writing and conversation
Structured progression according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (A1 to C1)
Methodical preparation for internationally recognised official exams

s-installer.title: Preparing your arrival and integration
s-installer.subtitle: Get ready for the practical, cultural and administrative realities of life in Europe.

sections.heading: The first formalities on arrival
sections.body: A successful move is prepared several months before departure: student housing, health insurance, registration with the local authority and opening a bank account.
bullets: Start looking for housing early through official university residences (e.g. Studierendenwerk)
Understand how residence registration (Anmeldung) and compulsory health insurance work
Know your rights and duties as a student or apprentice

eviter-les-arnaques.title: Avoiding scams and false promises
eviter-les-arnaques.subtitle: How to recognise a fraudulent offer, protect your loved ones and check every piece of information.

signes.title: You are promised a guaranteed visa
signes.text: Be wary of anyone who promises a visa that is “100% guaranteed” or “fast, with no interview at the embassy”. Decisions belong to the relevant authorities and institutions.

signes.title: Someone sells you a work or training contract
signes.text: A training (Ausbildung) or work contract in Europe can never be bought: it is the companies that pay the apprentice, never the other way round.

signes.title: You are promised admission without a diploma or language skills
signes.text: Studies and vocational training in Europe require a certified language level and, for studies, official recognition of your diplomas.

signes.title: You are asked to pay a private individual by mobile transfer
signes.text: No embassy or consulate asks for payment to a private individual by informal mobile transfer, and no member of WAHHF Foundation will ask you for money.

signes.title: A profile uses an official logo on a messaging app
signes.text: Watch out for fake profiles using official logos on WhatsApp, Telegram or Facebook: compare the number with our only official channels, at the top of this page.

fauxMessage.flag: 100% guaranteed visa for Germany, with no interview at the embassy.
fauxMessage.note: Be wary of any promise of a guaranteed visa or a visa without an interview: decisions belong to the relevant authorities and institutions.

fauxMessage.flag: A work contract is already waiting for you.
fauxMessage.note: A work or training contract can never be bought: it is the companies that recruit and pay.

fauxMessage.flag: send the application fee by mobile transfer
fauxMessage.note: Neither an embassy, nor a consulate, nor WAHHF Foundation asks for payment to a private individual.
A name or a logo proves nothing: compare the number with our only official channels.

promesses.title: A donation never gives access to a place
promesses.text: Donations fund the foundation’s actions. Making a donation reserves neither a place in our courses nor support.
No member, volunteer or partner of WAHHF will ask you for application, registration or deposit fees, or for payment by Mobile Money.
We do not ask for any identity document (passport, national ID card) at the first online contact.
We do not sell visas, plane tickets or work contracts.

reflexes.text: Always check the procedures on the official website of the embassy of the country concerned.
Never rely on unofficial pages: go directly to the institutional portals, listed on each country page.
If in doubt, stop the conversation immediately and report it to us, with a screenshot of the message.

allemagne.summary: Germany offers structured pathways for university studies, dual vocational training (Ausbildung) and skilled mobility.

pathways.studies: University admission (Studienkolleg, Bachelor’s, Master’s) depends on recognition of your diploma (Anabin / uni-assist), a B2/C1 level of German (or English, depending on the programme) and proof of the required financial resources.
pathways.training: Dual vocational training (Ausbildung), combining theory at school with an apprenticeship in a company, generally open from a B1/B2 level of German.
pathways.work: Professional mobility governed by the Skilled Immigration Act (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz), with recognition of qualifications.

steps: Learning German and obtaining an official language certificate (B1 to C1 depending on the project)
Checking the equivalence of your diplomas and putting together your academic or professional file
Applying to the educational or training institution
Booking an appointment and officially submitting your application to the competent German Embassy

officialLinks.label: Make it in Germany (official portal of the German Federal Government)
DAAD — German Academic Exchange Service
German Embassy in Cameroon (Yaoundé)

luxembourg.summary: In the heart of Europe, the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg offers a multilingual environment (French, German, English) for higher education and research.

pathways.studies: Bilingual or trilingual programmes at the University of Luxembourg, subject to academic admission requirements and student residence permit procedures.
pathways.training: Continuing education and academic internships governed by university agreements.
pathways.work: Residence permit for salaried workers issued by the Direction de l’immigration (Directorate of Immigration) before entering the country.

steps: Identifying the multilingual programme (French/German/English)
Submitting the university application within the official deadlines
Applying for a temporary authorisation to stay (ATS) from the competent ministry
Official consular formalities and preparing to settle in

officialLinks.label: Guichet.lu — Administrative portal of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
University of Luxembourg

slovenie.summary: A Central European country and member of the European Union, known for its public universities (Ljubljana, Maribor, Primorska) and its quality of student life.

pathways.studies: National eVŠ portal for applications to Slovenian universities at bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral level.
pathways.training: Academic exchanges, summer schools and technical internships.
pathways.work: Single residence and work permit managed by the Slovenian administrative units.

steps: Choosing the programme on the national academic portal eVŠ
Recognition procedure for previous diplomas
Preparing the application for a temporary residence permit for studies
Consular validation at the competent diplomatic mission

officialLinks.label: Study in Slovenia — Official portal
Government portal gov.si (Immigration)

italie.summary: With a long university tradition and regional scholarship programmes (DSU), Italy welcomes international students every year.

pathways.studies: Compulsory pre-enrolment on the official Universitaly platform, declaration of value (Dichiarazione di Valore) or CIMEA statement.
pathways.training: Higher technical training (ITS) and specialised schools.
pathways.work: Schemes regulated by the annual flow decrees (Decreto Flussi).

steps: Language preparation (Italian or English) and choosing a university
Pre-enrolment on the official Universitaly portal
Preparing academic and financial supporting documents
Submitting the study visa application to the Italian consular services

officialLinks.label: Universitaly — Official portal of the Italian Ministry
Visto per l’Italia — Ministry of Foreign Affairs

grece.summary: A Mediterranean crossroads and EU member, Greece is developing English-taught university programmes and courses in science, engineering and maritime studies.

pathways.studies: Public university programmes and international programmes coordinated by Study in Greece.
pathways.training: Vocational training in tourism, shipping and energy.
pathways.work: Residence and work permits according to the applicable agreements and the needs of each sector.

steps: Academic guidance and checking the language requirements
Application for admission to the Greek institution
Legalisation / apostille of academic documents
Official consular procedure at the competent Greek Embassy

officialLinks.label: Study in Greece — Official portal
Greek Ministry of Migration and Asylum

portugal.summary: Portugal offers a network of universities and polytechnic institutes recognised across Europe, with structured support for international students.

pathways.studies: Application under the international student status (Estatuto do Estudante Internacional) at universities and polytechnic institutes.
pathways.work: Work visa or job-seeker visa governed by AIMA and the Portuguese consular services.

steps: Learning basic Portuguese or obtaining an English certificate
Applying directly to the university or polytechnic institute
Obtaining the official letter of acceptance
Applying for a national study visa (D4) via the official Portuguese visa portal

officialLinks.label: Study & Research in Portugal — Official portal
Visa portal — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Portugal

espagne.summary: Spain has a vast network of public universities and higher vocational training centres (Formación Profesional de Grado Superior).

pathways.studies: University admission through homologation of your diploma or UNEDasiss accreditation.
pathways.training: Higher vocational training cycles (FP), much sought after in the technical and health sectors.
pathways.work: Procedures for an initial residence and salaried work authorisation.

steps: Academic homologation or accreditation procedure (UNEDasiss)
Pre-enrolment with the autonomous community or the chosen university
Putting together the complete consular file (insurance, financial resources, accommodation)
Submission to the competent Spanish Consulate

officialLinks.label: SEPIE — studying in Spain (Ministry of Universities)
Immigration portal — Government of Spain

danemark.summary: Known for its collaborative teaching and its English-taught programmes in engineering, renewable energy and life sciences.

pathways.studies: English-taught Bachelor’s and Master’s programmes, coordinated through the official Study in Denmark portal.
pathways.training: Academic internships and applied research programmes.
pathways.work: Schemes governed by the Danish Agency for International Recruitment and Integration (SIRI).

steps: Proving a high level of English (IELTS / TOEFL) and meeting the academic prerequisites
Applying via the national portal Optagelse.dk or directly to the university
Opening the ST1 application with the host institution
Applying for a residence permit from the official SIRI agency (nyidanmark.dk)

officialLinks.label: Study in Denmark — Official portal of the Ministry
New to Denmark (nyidanmark.dk) — Official SIRI portal

pologne.summary: A major academic and technological hub in Central Europe, Poland offers university programmes in English and Polish in science, medicine and computer science.

pathways.studies: Applications to public universities and technical universities, overseen by the national agency NAWA.
pathways.training: Preparatory language years and technical schools.
pathways.work: Work permit issued by the competent Voivodeship before applying for a national visa.

steps: Choosing an accredited institution on the government portal Study in Poland
Verification and apostille/legalisation of your secondary-school or higher-education diploma
Obtaining the official ministerial admission certificate
Consular registration via the official e-Konsulat system

officialLinks.label: Study in Poland — NAWA National Agency
Office for Foreigners of Poland (Urząd do Spraw Cudzoziemców)

albanie.euNote: Albania is not a member of the European Union (it has candidate country status). Nor is it part of the Schengen Area. Albanian visas and residence permits do not allow you to travel or work in the European Union.
albanie.summary: Located in the Western Balkans, Albania is developing accessible university programmes and regional exchange programmes, while falling under a national legal framework separate from that of the European Union.

pathways.studies: Enrolment at accredited public and private universities in Tirana and the country’s main cities.
pathways.training: Vocational training in regional development, tourism and technology.
pathways.work: Single permit applied for online via the government portal e-Albania.

steps: Understand that Albania is not a member of the EU
Obtain admission to an institution accredited by the ASCAL agency
Submit the type D visa application online on the official e-Visa portal of the Republic of Albania
Apply for a residence permit on e-Albania after your legal arrival

officialLinks.label: e-Visa Albania — Official online visa system
e-Albania — Official public services portal
